verdicts.summary: [N] nasqret/z-in-q-lean states a different claim; neither implies the other (differs).
evidence: Pstar_spec and assembly state the target for ndep's specPstar, whose embedded pole template uses the curves x+l in place of [M]'s x+3l, so the polynomial differs; [N] has no assembly lemma for [M]'s P_* of its own. The hypotheses also include Compiler.NodeCheck.HaltingAddMulBound, not named in the note.

Survives: [N] never names the specified P_* (no Pstar/specPstar anywhere in nasqret/); its own assembly theorems conclude only IntegerPolynomial (some polynomial, no bounds or variable count) or ZInQ.FrozenTarget (some polynomial with [M]'s bounds), both existential and weaker than 'P_* satisfies Theorem 1.1'. The rank inputs replacing PC are theorem-standing hypotheses and do not rescue the conclusion; PublicAssembly.frozen_of_geometry_and_genus is also only FrozenTarget.

No [N] declaration names ndep's specPstar or Pstar_spec (grep of nasqret for Pstar finds nothing); [N]'s assembly theorems conclude only the existential IntegerPolynomial (no bounds) or ndep's existential FrozenTarget, under UniformHeight/SixContactMin and a Tian/Gross-Zagier rank input, so the conclusion about the specified P_* is indeed missing and the claim stands.
